paper.title: Revisiting Clustering of Neural Bandits: Selective Reinitialization for Mitigating Loss of Plasticity

settings.name_in_paper: Clustering of Neural Bandits (CNB) in the piecewise-stationary setting
unmapped: n users, each a bandit with its own (nonlinear) reward function g_{u,t}; users are grouped into item-dependent clusters ((eps1,eps2)-user clusters)
a user u_t arrives each round and K arms with d-dimensional features are offered
reward function changes abruptly at S change points (piecewise stationary)

algorithms.name: SeRe-enhanced CNB (Selective Reinitialization with Page-Hinkley-Absolute change detection)

symbols.S_T: number of change points / pieces S in the piecewise-stationary environment (paper's S)

conditions: NTK over-parameterized regime: network width m >= poly(T, L, 1/delta) and trained parameters stay within a radius R of initialization
feature vectors satisfy ||a||_2 <= 1; rewards g in [0,1]; noise 1-sub-Gaussian conditioned on history
Assumption (c): change detection triggers reinitialization within a bounded delay Delta after each change point (Delta treated as a constant)
Assumption (d): reinitialization restores the random-feature properties so NTK analysis applies in each new segment
S << T (S term dominated by sqrt(ST))

source.label: thm:SeRe_sublinear_main
source.quote: For SeRe-enhanced CNB algorithms, in the piecewise-stationary setting of \(S\) pieces, the cumulative dynamic regret over \(T\) rounds satisfies \[ \mathbf{R}_T = \sum_{s=0}^S \mathbf{R}_s = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\Bigl(\sqrt{T S}\Bigr). \] In particular, if the number of pieces satisfies \(S = o(T)\) ..., then the overall regret is sublinear in \(T\).

results.notes: Theorem statement does not specify probability; the appendix proof gives, w.p. >= 1-delta, R_T <= S*Delta + C sqrt(d_eff (S+1) T log(T(S+1)/delta)) with d_eff the NTK effective dimension, hidden in O-tilde. Proof relies on strong assumptions (bounded detection delay, effective reinitialization) and heuristic arguments. Paper's S (number of shifts) renamed S_T.

cited_results.setting_description: Clustering of neural bandits in a single stationary period of length H, NTK regime, rewards in [0,1], 1-sub-Gaussian noise; high-probability regret
